data.name: Mursid
data.gender_notes: Mursid is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is deeply devoted to Lord Muruga, a deity in Hindu mythology. Muruga is known for his bravery and intelligence, and his devotees seek his blessings for strength and wisdom. The name Mursid carries the meaning “Lord Muruga's devotee” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mursid usually hope their child will grow to embody lord muruga's devotee and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies deep devotion to Lord Muruga, symbolizing strength, wisdom, and divine protection.
data.etymology: Mursid belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord Muruga's devotee.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mursid total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

historical_references.reference: Mursid was a Hindu king of the Chalukya Dynasty, ruling from Vatapi (present day Badami) from 542 to 545 CE. He is known for his military conquests and architectural achievements, including the construction of the Vascular Temple.
Mursid Qadri is a Sufi saint from the 13th century. He was a disciple of Shah Jalal and is known for his contributions to Sufism and spreading Islamic teachings in Bengal.
